doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Lou Rawls band, Alias and Jaco
title: How busy the Rawls band was and what he earned
summary: Rawls worked constantly, especially the first year. Montalbano earned four or five hundred dollars a week and saved money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Right. How was Lou Rawls’ work from the time you joined the band? Did it stay consistent?

He worked a lot. He worked like crazy, especially the first year. Yeah. And it was a ball. We had a great time. He was a ball to work with. He liked to work. He liked to be out there working. He had gone through a divorce I guess and needed to make some money.
Do you recall what you were making at that time, if you don’t mind my asking? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -12-

Maybe four or five hundred dollars a week, which was a lot of money back then. Oh my God. When I came off of the road I had so much money saved, and I spent a lot of money. You know I had probably a hundred dollar a week phone bills back then calling home to my wife. And I always managed to put money away and I had a little nest egg.
